![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14121463/assets/33e48fa5bdbb034bcf489e038ccf80fc5f67baabeccacc1b7abd741183ebf05d.png)

Consider the square region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 1},
$$

and the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:(u,v)\to (x(u,v),y(u,v)),
$$

where 

$$
x={u}^{2}-{v}^{2},\,y=1-u+v.
$$

Which of the following is the image of the side ${S}_{2}$ under the action of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
To map the entire region $Δ$ onto the $xy$-plane, we consider the transformation of each side. However, in this case, we consider only the side ${S}_{2}.$

For the side ${S}_{2},$ we have $u=1$ and $0\le v\le 1.$ Substituting $u=1$ into our transformation equations, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y) & =T(u,v) \\  & =({u}^{2}-{v}^{2},\,1-u+v) \\  & =({1}^{2}-{v}^{2},\,1-1+v) \\  & =(1-{v}^{2},\,v).\end{aligned}
$$

So, the image of ${S}_{2}$ can be parametrized by

$$
x=1-{v}^{2},\,y=v,\,0\le v\le 1.
$$

 

Writing this in the usual notation, we have

$$
x=1-{t}^{2},\,y=t,\,0\le t\le 1.
$$

These are parametric equations of a parabolic arc. Notice that if we eliminate $t$ from the equations, we get

$$
x=1-{y}^{2}\,⇒\,{y}^{2}=1-x
$$

which is a left-opening parabola whose vertex is at $(1,0).$

Moreover, the endpoints of ${S}_{2}$ are mapped to the $xy$-plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & T:(1,0)\to ({1}^{2}-{0}^{2},1-1+0)=(1,0) \\  & T:(1,1)\to ({1}^{2}-{1}^{0},1-1+1)=(0,1)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the image of ${S}_{2}$ is an arc of a left-opening parabola, traversed from $(1,0)$ to $(0,1).$

An arc of a left-opening parabola, traversed from $(1,0)$ to $(0,1).$
An arc of a downward-opening parabola, traversed from $(2,1)$ to $(1,1).$
An arc of a left-opening parabola, traversed from $(0,1)$ to $(1,0).$
An arc of a downward-opening parabola, traversed from $(1,1)$ to $(2,1).$

responses.value: An arc of a downward-opening parabola, traversed from $(1,0)$ to $(0,1).$
